items.definition: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for a job or a place on a course.
examples: I've applied for three jobs this week.

items.definition: The series of jobs a person does in one area of work during their working life.
examples: She had a long career in journalism.

trap.en: A university course is a degree, not a career. I'm studying law, not I'm studying the career of law.
trap.es: «Estudio la carrera de Derecho» se dice I'm studying law o I'm doing a law degree. Career es la trayectoria profesional.

items.definition: A person who works in the same place or organisation as you.
examples: I usually have lunch with my colleagues.

items.definition: To travel regularly between home and work.
examples: I commute to Manchester by train every day.

items.definition: A day when you do not go to work, although it is a normal working day.
examples: I'm taking a day off on Friday to move house.

items.definition: The time or day by which a piece of work must be finished.
examples: We're working late to meet the deadline.

items.definition: Working for several different organisations rather than being employed by one.
Time worked beyond your normal hours, or the extra money paid for it.
examples: I did ten hours' overtime last week.

items.definition: A move to a more important job in the same organisation.
examples: She got a promotion after only a year.

items.definition: To find new people to work for an organisation or join a group.
examples: The hospital is struggling to recruit nurses.

items.definition: No longer employed because your job is no longer needed.
examples: Two hundred staff were made redundant when the factory closed.

items.definition: To leave a job officially, because you have decided to.
examples: He resigned from the board in protest.

items.definition: A period of work that starts when another group of workers finishes.
The amount of work a person or organisation has to do.
examples: My workload has doubled since my colleague left.
